title: Ethiopian Lentil Soup
community: All of Ethiopia — the thin lentil soup
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Lentil Soup — a thinner, more soup-like version of Misir Wat, drunk as a warming soup on cold highland evenings and during fasting periods. The berbere lentil soup — same flavours as Misir Wat but in a pourable form.
longDesc: Ethiopian lentil soup is the pourable version of Misir Wat — the same berbere-onion base with more water added, producing a warming soup rather than a thick stew. Drunk from cups on cold Addis Ababa evenings.
ingredients: Lemon wedges and coriander to serve
steps: Make the base as per Misir Wat — dry-caramelise onions, fry berbere.
Add lentils and water (more water than Misir Wat).
For a smooth soup: blend partially or fully.
Season. Serve with lemon and coriander.
chefTips: More water than Misir Wat — should be pourable.
Lemon squeezed at the table brightens the soup significantly.
sustainabilityTips: Red lentils — very low environmental impact.
servedWith: With injera for a light meal
healthBenefits: Warming — ideal for highland cold evenings.
culturalNote: Ethiopian lentil soup is the warming drink of fasting evenings — when the cold descends on the Ethiopian highlands and the family gathers, a pot of berbere lentil soup heating on the fire is the most comforting thing possible.
